LESSON: LINES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: THEME: OUR MARKET Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learnin
Topic 4.1: Lines
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Lines, part of THEME: OUR MARKET Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learnin in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why are the objects different from each other?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Observe concrete objects (books, charts, woodblocks, string/ropes) /models of objects found in the market and talk about lines found in them in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication (AAC) or use residual speech or be lip-read by peers, learner support assistance or teacher as they talk about lines found in objects.

2. Cooperate with others to form lines by arranging concrete objects one after the other, modelling or joining dots as they observe safety.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Observe concrete objects (books, charts, woodblocks, string/ropes) /models of objects found in the market and talk about lines found in them in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication (AAC) or use residual speech or be lip-read by peers, learner support assistance or teacher as they talk about lines found in objects.
2. Cooperate with others to form lines by arranging concrete objects one after the other, modelling or joining dots as they observe safety.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Lines together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Citizenship: learners bond socially as they work together to identify and form lines.

Values:
Unity: learners amicably work together to identify and form lines.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: learners carefully arrange concrete objects to form lines.

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate joining dots to form lines to joining dots to form pictures in Creative Activities.
